title: Tamil-Born Dr. Q. Manivannan Makes History at Holyrood
excerpt: The Indian-origin Scottish Green MSP becomes one of Scotland's first openly transgender parliamentarians in the 2026 elections.
body:
A Tamil-born doctoral researcher just made history inside Scotland's Parliament. Dr. Q. Manivannan, a nonbinary Indian-origin politician, won a regional list seat for Edinburgh and Lothians East in the 2026 Scottish Parliament election held on 7 May, with results declared on 8 May — becoming one of the first openly transgender Members of the Scottish Parliament (MSPs) in the legislature's 27-year history.

**Who Is Dr. Q. Manivannan:**
Born in Tamil Nadu and educated at O.P. Jindal Global University in Delhi, Manivannan later completed an MPhil in international peace studies at Trinity College Dublin before arriving in Scotland in 2021 to pursue an ESRC-funded doctorate in international relations at the University of St Andrews. They ran as third on the Scottish Green Party's Edinburgh and Lothians East regional list — and the Greens' strong performance pushed them across the threshold into Parliament.

**The Visa Question and the Historic Win:**
Manivannan does not hold British citizenship or permanent residency, but stood as a Commonwealth citizen — a legally valid basis under Scottish electoral rules. Questions emerged about their student visa's work-hour restrictions, but the Scottish Greens swiftly confirmed that Manivannan held 'a valid visa with the right to work and live in Scotland.' Addressing jubilant supporters at Edinburgh's Royal Highland Centre, they declared: 'I am a transgender Tamil immigrant' — a moment that resonated far beyond Holyrood. Fellow Green MSP Iris Duane was simultaneously elected in Glasgow, making them the two firsts together.

**What to Watch:**
All eyes now turn to Manivannan's visa transition — they were fundraising for a graduate visa before the election — and whether the Scottish Parliament's Session 7, due to meet first on 14 May 2026, will address the broader questions of migrant representation in UK devolved politics.

nri_angle: For Indian-Americans who have navigated the complex intersection of immigration status, identity, and civic participation, Dr. Manivannan's election as a Tamil immigrant without permanent residency — winning a seat in a European parliament through Commonwealth citizenship rights — is a direct and powerful reminder of how diasporic political belonging can be redefined.
